channel.title: NewsCenter — Top 5 news of the day — 2026-11-26
channel.description: The five news that matter most today, chosen from Laurent's newsletters. 110 news received.

item.title: 1. FCC authorizes SpaceX’s one-million-unit AI satellite network
item.description: Why it matters: The FCC’s approval of SpaceX’s planned one-million-satellite AI network could reshape space infrastructure, cloud computing, spectrum competition and astronomical regulation. The FCC approved Starmind, SpaceX’s project to launch up to one million solar-powered satellites equipped with AI data centers. Despite opposition from Amazon, Viasat, and astronomers, the first launches are planned for 2027 and the network must be completed by 2040.

item.title: 2. Anthropic Shares Fall Below Their IPO Price
item.description: Why it matters: Anthropic shares falling below their IPO price is an important market test of whether frontier-AI revenues can justify enormous computing and operating costs. Anthropic shares fell below their IPO price less than a week after going public, suggesting investors still doubt that revenue will exceed costs.

item.title: 3. HPE shares fall as AI-related margin decline weighs
item.description: Why it matters: HPE’s sharp share-price decline shows that surging AI-server demand may not translate into profits when component costs rise faster than vendors’ pricing power. HPE shares fell about 16%, as margin guidance overshadowed an improved forecast for 2027 revenue growth. Demand for AI servers is supporting revenue, but component costs are rising faster than selling prices.

item.title: 4. Chinese labs estimate they are up to nine months behind the United States
item.description: Why it matters: Chinese AI labs reportedly being within nine months of U.S. leaders despite chip restrictions highlights the limits of export controls and the intensity of strategic competition. Chip restrictions, limited access to Nvidia hardware and anti-distillation measures are weighing on DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Alibaba. DeepSeek researchers reportedly estimate internally that they are no more than nine months behind.

item.title: 5. OpenAI tests private inference for businesses
item.description: Why it matters: OpenAI’s private-inference trials could remove a major data-confidentiality barrier to enterprise adoption of frontier AI models. OpenAI’s Private Inference runs a company’s queries on its best models without OpenAI being able to see the data. The service is being tested with early business customers.
